title: intent critic reports 'no staged elixir files to scan' when it means 'no coverage for the files you staged' -- 60 .heex files across three fleet estates read as nothing to scan
body:
FOUND BY prolix-cc, 2026-08-24, as a side observation. The diagnosis below is
vc's and it contradicts the obvious fix.

WHAT HAPPENS. `intent critic elixir --staged` prints

    no staged elixir files to scan

while `.heex` files are staged. prolix-cc lost three heex-only rule fixes to
this in one session: none was examined and nothing said so.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS A NO-OP. `bin/intent_critic:199` reads
`elixir:*.ex|elixir:*.exs)` and `foo.heex` does not match `*.ex`, so the filter
is the visible half. But NOT ONE ELIXIR RULE DECLARES A GLOB THAT REACHES
`.heex`: the pack carries five distinct globs -- `lib/**/*.ex`,
`lib/**/controllers/**/*.ex`, `lib/**/live/**/*.ex`, `test/**/*_test.exs`,
`test/support/**/*.ex` -- and every one excludes it. Passing heex through the
filter would feed it to rules that reject it.

SO HEEX COVERAGE WAS NEVER BUILT, RATHER THAN BUILT AND BROKEN. Whether it
should exist is a rules-authoring decision -- which existing rules apply to a
template, and whether heex needs its own -- and not a one-line filter fix.
Adding the extension without the authoring work would convert a silent gap into
a silent no-op, which is strictly worse: the message would stop appearing while
the coverage still would not exist.

THE DEFECT THAT SURVIVES THAT DIAGNOSIS IS THE MESSAGE, AND IT IS REAL.
"no staged elixir files to scan" describes the wrong thing. There ARE staged
files the operator considers Elixir; what is absent is COVERAGE. A reader takes
it as coverage, which is exactly how three fixes went unexamined.

THIS IS 0069's FAMILY, ONE DOOR OVER: a line reporting a fixed noun rather than
what the operation actually did. 0069 is `sync`'s confirmation counting threads
regardless of what changed; this is `critic`'s counting FILES IT RECOGNISES and
saying "files". A correct message here names the gap: staged files that no rule
in this pack can reach.

BLAST RADIUS, measured 2026-08-24 rather than argued: 30 `.heex` in Lamplight,
21 in Anvil, 9 in Conflab. 60 files across three flagship Elixir estates, all
invisible to the gate, all reporting as nothing to scan.

TWO SEPARABLE DECISIONS, and they should not be bundled:
  1. The MESSAGE should distinguish "no staged files" from "no coverage for the
     staged files". That is a defect in any case and needs no authoring ruling.
  2. Whether the elixir pack should cover `.heex` at all is hv's, and it is
     work rather than a fix.
